A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HOI-Dyn with matching core methods and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and relocated or renumbered content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original HOI-Dyn benchmark results, architecture and guidance ablations, residual-loss comparisons, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original HOI-Dyn experiments and adds numerical evaluations without object waypoints and with perturbed dynamics-model inputs.

M1.justification: The dynamics transformer, conditional diffusion model, residual dynamics loss, loss weighting, and guidance procedures are retained. The nonresidual-loss equation in Appendix C.3 documents a variant already evaluated in v1 Appendix G; the physics-surrogate discussion does not introduce another model.

E1.justification: V3 adds generation without object waypoints, changing the conditioning requirements within the existing HOI domain. FullBodyManipulation, 3D-FUTURE, and the Replica scene application already appear in v1; moving the scene application into Section 4.3 does not introduce a new dataset.

E2.justification: The evaluated external baselines remain InterDiff, MDM, OMOMO variants, and CHOIS. V3's loss ablation retains CHOIS and the residual/nonresidual variants from v1. Its new waypoint experiment uses CHOIS again; newly discussed methods such as HIMO and ChainHOI are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The new no-waypoint evaluation excludes inference guidance and waypoint/GT errors, while reporting diversity and broader penetration measurements. Appendix E.2 introduces normalized input perturbations at five scales from 10^-5 to 10^-1. The residual-loss comparison is restricted to unguided results and fewer metrics. Existing benchmark splits, model sizes, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds direct diagnostics of two important premises: dependence on waypoint conditioning (Table 5) and local smoothness under input perturbations (Appendix E.2, Tables 8–9). It also expands the scene case study with a box example. The residual-loss ablation already existed in v1 Appendix G; v3 integrates its unguided subset into Appendix C.3 and removes the guided nonresidual comparison.

E5.justification: Table 3's uncertainty entries, the existing plot error bars, Appendix C.2's residual statistics, and the checklist's statistical-significance description are retained. V3 supplies no new run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance-test specifications, or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their values. New results include no-waypoint FID scores of 4.81 for HOI-Dyn versus 5.36 for CHOIS, perturbation-response measurements, and the box scene example. Some residual-ablation entries are removed. V3 Table 7 changes baseline foot sliding to 3.63, conflicting with 0.57 in v1 Table 6 and v3 Table 4; 3.63 is the corresponding FID value.

T1.justification: The synchronization equations and Appendix C.1 residual-error derivation are unchanged. Appendix E.2 adds an explicit Lipschitz condition and mathematical definitions of normalized perturbations and output deviation in Eqs. 31–32. This is a limited formal addition supporting the sensitivity test, rather than a new bias-cancellation proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: the driver-responder formulation, lightweight dynamics transformer, residual supervision without additional generation-time cost, improved HOI synthesis, and dynamics-based evaluation. The expanded conclusion does not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations of the predictor as a differentiable physics surrogate and conditional world model, explains the smoothness/time-homogeneity rationale, and discusses the residual-loss ablation explicitly. The rigid-object and coarse-hand limitations remain; multi-human and multi-object scalability is added as future work.

D1.justification: V1 promises code release after acceptance, whereas v3 provides project and repository links and reports code availability in checklist item 5, substantially changing documented access. Section 4 also newly discloses scheduler parameters T0=20, Tmult=1, and eta_min=10^-5. These disclosures do not establish changed training settings, and repository functionality cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially revises positioning around object-guided versus joint HOI generation and adds HIMO and ChainHOI. Appendix C.4 introduces comparisons with PhysHOI, InterMimic, SkillMimic, and FORCE to position learned dynamics against physics simulation. Adam and Replica references are added, while the earlier general human-motion survey reference is removed.

P1.justification: The related-work narrative is extensively rewritten and reordered. The scene application moves from Appendix D.2 to Section 4.3, the former Appendix G ablation is integrated into Appendix C.3, and the checklist moves before the appendices. Appendices A, C, and E gain explanatory subsections; author information and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: V3 adds Tables 5, 8, and 9 and redesigns v1 Table 6 as the narrower Table 7. The scene illustration becomes a main-text figure with reformatted lamp frames and an additional box panel. Existing dynamics plots receive typography and line-style adjustments, while most other graphical content is retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: The added waypoint-removal and perturbation tests address gaps in v1's validation, while clearer research positioning and additional reproducibility information provide a limited net gain. These benefits are tempered by removal of guided nonresidual results and the erroneous baseline foot-sliding entry in Table 7. The core method, principal benchmark results, and residual-bias derivation remain unchanged.
